t.1.196.1: O king, we have heard it said that those who are summoned for counsel and who are devoted to the welfare of Dhṛtarāṣṭra should speak what is righteous, beneficial and conducive to glory.
t.1.196.3: Let some sweet-spoken man be sent quickly to Drupada, taking abundant treasure on their behalf, O Bhārata.
t.1.196.2: My view too, dear one, is the same as that of the great-souled Bhīṣma: the Kaunteyas must be given their share, for this is the eternal dharma.
t.1.196.4: Let that man go to him, taking many things fitting for their mutual alliance, and let him likewise speak of the supreme prosperity that will arise from that union.
t.1.196.6: He should describe again and again the fitness and the agreeableness of the alliance, while conciliating the sons of Kuntī and the two sons of Mādrī.
t.1.196.5: Let him tell Drupada and Dhṛṣṭadyumna again and again, O king, O Bhārata, that you are well pleased, and Duryodhana likewise.
t.1.196.7: At your command, O king of kings, let him present to Draupadī many bright ornaments of gold.
t.1.196.8: Likewise, O bull of the Bharatas, whatever gifts are fitting for all the sons of Drupada and for all the Pāṇḍavas, and those that are fitting for Kuntī as well.
t.1.196.10: When the heroes have been granted leave, let a splendid army go forth; let Duḥśāsana and Vikarṇa bring the Pāṇḍavas here.
t.1.196.9: Having thus addressed Drupada, together with the Pāṇḍavas, in words full of conciliation, he should then speak about their coming.
t.1.196.12: Thus, great king, I consider such conduct on your part toward those sons, together with Bhīṣma, to be fitting, O Bhārata.
t.1.196.13: These two, bound to you by wealth and honour and close to you in every affair, would not counsel what is good for you. What could be more astonishing than that?
t.1.196.14: He who, with a corrupt mind and a concealed inner self, would speak of what is supposedly the highest good, how could he carry out the counsel of the virtuous?
t.1.196.16: Whether a man be wise or unwise, a child or an old man, with allies or without allies, he obtains everything everywhere.
t.1.196.15: In times of hardship, friends are not the cause of one's good or of its opposite; for everyone's sorrow, or else happiness, comes about as ordained by fate.
t.1.196.17: For it is heard that long ago there was a certain king in Rājagṛha, known as Ambuvīca, a king among the Māgadha rulers of the earth.
t.1.196.18: Deprived of all his faculties, with nothing left to him but his breath, that king then came to depend on his ministers in all affairs.
t.1.196.20: Then that deluded one took for himself everything that belonged to the king, his objects of enjoyment, his women, his jewels and wealth, and his sovereignty as well.
t.1.196.19: Formerly his minister Mahākarṇi became the sole lord; regarding himself as one who had gained power, he treats the king with contempt.
t.1.196.21: And when he had taken that, the greed of the greedy one only grew with his gain; and so, having taken everything, he now wishes to seize his kingdom as well.
t.1.196.23: What else, surely, was that lordship of men of his but what was ordained? If the kingdom is ordained for you, O lord of the people, it will be yours.
t.1.196.25: Thus, O wise one, discern the goodness and wickedness of your counsellors; the speech both of the corrupt and of the uncorrupted must be understood.
t.1.196.24: While the whole world looks on, that will surely abide in you; but if it has been ordained otherwise than this, you will not obtain it even though you strive.
t.1.196.22: Though he strove for it, he could not seize the kingdom of that king, who was bereft of all his faculties and had nothing left but his breath; so we have heard.
t.1.196.26: We know, from the corruption of your disposition, why this is being said by you: malicious because of the Pāṇḍavas, you are proclaiming a fault in us.
t.1.196.27: But, Karṇa, I speak what is of the highest benefit, what will make the Kurus prosper. If you consider it wrong, then tell me what is the highest good.
t.1.196.28: If anything other than this, which I declare to be the highest good, is done, the Kurus will perish before long; such is my conviction.
t.1.196.11: Then, O best of kings, always honored by you, they will stand in their ancestral position with the consent of the people.
